artifacts.summary: Compares the four candidate mechanisms for the typst/generated/status.typ staleness gap; recommends a versioned pre-commit hook (build-free --json gate that blocks the commit and prints the fix command, avoiding both the built-library requirement and the spurious-stamp-diff hazard) plus a --fix mode on typst-sync-check.sh as a complementary manual remedy; rejects compile-time computation as infeasible under Typst's sandboxing; notes the .claude/ agent-orchestrator reading of option (c) is out of this repo's boundary but is subsumed by the recommended hook since git-commit-scoped.sh never bypasses hooks.

memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic, a generated-artifact freshness gate (typst-sync-check.sh Check 2) that only detects drift in CI, with no local hook ever calling the generator, recurs as a failure class even though the fix is a single documented command -- because nothing ever prompts anyone to run it. The general pattern: when a checker and generator already agree and the only defect is 'nothing calls the generator', prefer a build-free (--json-mode) blocking pre-commit gate that only pays the expensive/build-dependent regeneration cost when a real mismatch is found, and never auto-regenerates+restages silently (which would create spurious diffs from unrelated stamp/timestamp fields).

In BimodalLogic, .claude/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh (the orchestrator's sanctioned committer) invokes a plain `git commit` with no --no-verify anywhere. This means any versioned repo-local git hook (once core.hooksPath points at it) fires transparently for both human and orchestrator-driven commits alike -- a useful lever for closing gaps that would otherwise require editing the .claude/ agent-system source store (which is a separate repository and off-limits per source-store-deploy-boundary.md).
